# Task Summary

Plan `PK-001 Home Experience` for the `/` route only. Replace the starter landing page with a product-specific home experience that explains PokeAtlas, highlights a curated Pokemon spotlight, and exposes primary entry points for browse, compare, and team-building flows without implementing those downstream routes.

# Affected Area Summary

- `src/app/page.tsx`
  - Replace the starter page with the home experience shell and section composition.
- `src/app/layout.tsx`
  - Update static metadata so the app title and description match the product.

  - Introduce a small set of global tokens/utilities for the landing page visual system and remove the Arial body override so the existing `next/font` setup is effective.

# Implementation Approach

Use a server-rendered marketing-style composition for `/` with static content only. The page should include:

- a hero that states what PokeAtlas is and what users can do here
- a quick-entry section with three primary journeys
- a curated spotlight card or panel for one featured Pokemon
- a short supporting explainer that reinforces browsing, comparison, and team-building use cases

Implementation guidance:

- Keep `src/app/page.tsx` as a React Server Component.
- Avoid adding `'use client'` unless the chosen CTA behavior requires client-only interaction.
- Keep featured content static and local to this feature; no fetches, route handlers, or server actions.
- Prefer extracting section blocks into `src/components/home/*` rather than accumulating a single large page file.
- Use `next/image` only for local assets if imagery is added. Do not introduce remote image dependencies in this chunk.
- Keep the CTA layer shallow: copy, links, and affordances only. Do not stub full browse/detail/team-builder functionality under this feature.

# Architecture Notes

- Server/client boundary:
  - Default boundary stays entirely server-side.
  - If CTAs are non-navigational placeholders, they should remain semantic and accessible without introducing client state unless there is a concrete interaction requirement.
- Data placement:
  - Spotlight and quick-entry content should live in local static constants or server-safe presentational props.
  - No async data fetching is needed.
- Metadata:
  - Static metadata should be defined in `src/app/layout.tsx` for product name, description, and social-preview-ready copy baseline.
- Styling:
  - Prefer a limited set of reusable CSS custom properties or Tailwind-driven utility patterns in `globals.css` for gradients, surfaces, and accent colors rather than one-off inline class sprawl.
- Component composition:
  - Favor explicit section components such as hero, spotlight, and entry cards over boolean-prop-heavy shared blocks.
  - Keep section components presentational and stateless.
- UX/accessibility:
  - Preserve heading hierarchy.
  - Ensure CTA links/buttons have visible focus states and descriptive labels.
  - Treat decorative imagery as decorative; do not add meaningless alt text.
